forms.label: Asking if an item is available
forms.japanese: 今日のランチセットはありますか
forms.english: Is there a set lunch today?
forms.explanation: 「〜はありますか」asks whether something is available. 今日のランチセット is the topic being asked about, marked by は. ありますか is the polite question form of あります (there is / we have it).

forms.label: Requesting an item
forms.japanese: カレーをお願いします
forms.explanation: 「〜をお願いします」is a polite way to request something. カレー is the item requested, marked by を.

forms.label: Saying you need an item
forms.explanation: 「〜が必要です」means something is needed. スプーン is the needed item, marked by が.

speakingObjectives: Ask whether there is a set lunch today.
wordBank: 今日のランチセットはありますか
カレーをお願いします
スプーンをお願いします

forms.label: Stating a destination
forms.english: I am going to the dining hall
forms.explanation: 「〜に行きます」means go to a place. 食堂 is the destination, marked by に.

forms.label: Stating what you will order
forms.explanation: カレー is the object of the verb, marked by を. 注文します is the polite form of order, used here for a future action.

forms.label: Asking about card payment
forms.explanation: で marks the means of payment. 払えます is the polite potential form of 払う (to pay), meaning can pay. か makes it a question.

speakingObjectives: Tell a companion where you will eat.
Ask the staff whether you can pay by card.

forms.label: Stating what you eat
forms.japanese: わたしはサラダを食べます
forms.explanation: は marks わたし as the topic. サラダ is the thing eaten, marked by を. 食べます is the polite form of eat.

forms.label: か in a proposal to share
forms.explanation: を marks the salad as the item to share. か makes the polite 分けます question a proposal in this context.

forms.label: Stating how you will pay
forms.explanation: 「で」marks the means of payment. 払います is the polite form of pay.

speakingObjectives: Ask whether your companion eats avocado.
wordBank: わたしはサラダを食べます
アボカドは食べますか
